topic.title: Kernel Learning and Statistical Function Estimation
topic.overview: Kernel methods learn functions through similarity relationships, with behavior governed by the geometry of a function space. This cluster studies effective dimension, regularization, low-rank and random-feature approximations, distribution shift, and uncertainty bounds. It also includes methods for indefinite similarities that fall outside ordinary positive-definite kernel assumptions.
topic.whyItMatters: Choosing a similarity function determines which patterns a learner can express and how much data it needs. Computational approximations and uncertainty estimates must respect that structure if kernel methods are to remain useful on large or noisy datasets.
topic.evolution: The collection spans early links between neural and kernel representations through effective-dimension analyses and scalable approximations. Later work extends learning to indefinite spaces and shifted distributions. Recent papers develop fast structured kernels and uniform regression bounds that accommodate heavier-tailed or correlated noise, broadening both computational and statistical applicability.
openQuestions: How can an approximation budget be matched to the effective dimension of a task?
Which uncertainty guarantees remain informative under realistic dependence and distribution shift?

papers.title: Overfitting Behaviour of Gaussian Kernel Ridgeless Regression: Varying Bandwidth or Dimensionality
papers.tldr: Under stated universality and non-rigorous risk assumptions, the paper characterizes when Gaussian kernel interpolation overfits and when growing dimension permits benign overfitting.

papers.title: Scalable Kernel Inverse Optimization
papers.tldr: Kernel Inverse Optimization learns richer expert objectives through a finite convex reformulation and a training algorithm designed to improve scalability.

papers.title: Statistical and Geometrical properties of the Kernel Kullback-Leibler divergence
papers.tldr: A regularized kernel KL divergence handles disjoint supports and comes with statistical bounds, a finite-sample formula, and a transport scheme.

papers.title: Supervised Kernel Thinning
papers.tldr: Supervised kernel thinning accelerates two kernel regression methods while offering better statistical efficiency than independent random subsampling.

papers.title: The Minimax Rate of HSIC Estimation for Translation-Invariant Kernels
papers.tldr: The paper proves an optimal n⁻¹ᐟ² worst-case rate for HSIC estimation under specified kernel and distribution assumptions, validating several common estimators.

papers.title: Joker: Joint Optimization Framework for Lightweight Kernel Machines
papers.tldr: Joker combines randomized kernel features with joint optimization to support several kernel models while saving up to 90% memory in experiments.

papers.title: K$^2$IE: Kernel Method-based Kernel Intensity Estimators for Inhomogeneous Poisson Processes
papers.tldr: K²IE connects classical intensity estimation with RKHS optimization and uses that connection to improve computational efficiency.

papers.title: Kernel Quantile Embeddings and Associated Probability Metrics
papers.tldr: Kernel quantile embeddings yield efficiently estimated distribution distances with metric guarantees under weaker kernel conditions than MMD.

papers.title: Learning with Exact Invariances in Polynomial Time
papers.tldr: Given a geometric oracle, the proposed kernel-learning algorithm achieves exact invariance in polynomial time while preserving the original excess-risk guarantee.

papers.title: Low-Rank Thinning
papers.tldr: A low-rank analysis broadens thinning guarantees and improves theoretical results for attention approximation, training reordering, and distribution comparison.

papers.title: One-Pass Feature Evolvable Learning with Theoretical Guarantees
papers.tldr: A kernel-based measure of relationships between changing feature spaces enables one-pass learning without retaining training examples.

papers.title: Anchor-based Maximum Discrepancy for Relative Similarity Testing
papers.tldr: AMD jointly learns a similarity hypothesis and a deep kernel, then tests the hypothesis’s statistical significance.

papers.title: Computational Efficiency under Covariate Shift in Kernel Ridge Regression
papers.tldr: Random subspaces can reduce kernel regression’s computational burden while preserving learning performance under covariate shift.

papers.title: DUAL: Learning Diverse Kernels for Aggregated Two-sample and Independence Testing
papers.tldr: DUAL combines diverse, individually effective kernels to strengthen statistical tests while providing theoretical false-positive control.

papers.title: Fast Training of Large Kernel Models with Delayed Projections
papers.tldr: EP4 delays projections in preconditioned stochastic gradient descent to train larger kernel models much faster without sacrificing reported performance.

papers.title: Kernel conditional tests from learning-theoretic bounds
papers.tldr: The paper converts learning-theoretic confidence bounds into practical kernel tests that identify where conditional distributions or their properties differ.

papers.title: Kernel Regression in Structured Non-IID Settings: Theory and Implications for Denoising Score Learning
papers.tldr: The paper derives kernel-regression generalization bounds for noisy views of shared signals and applies them to denoising score learning.

papers.title: Kernel von Mises Formula of the Influence Function
papers.tldr: A kernel spectral representation enables influence-function estimation without manual analytical derivation and comes with a consistency proof.

papers.title: Learning Theory for Kernel Bilevel Optimization
papers.tldr: The paper develops finite-sample generalization bounds for kernel bilevel optimization and uses them to analyze the statistical accuracy of gradient-based methods.

papers.title: Practical Kernel Selection for Kernel-based Conditional Independence Test
papers.tldr: The paper selects KCI kernel parameters through a parallelizable criterion tied to large-sample test power, with theoretical and empirical support.

papers.title: Regularized least squares learning with heavy-tailed noise is minimax optimal
papers.tldr: Kernel ridge regression achieves minimax-optimal convergence rates under heavy-tailed noise with suitable finite moments and standard eigenvalue-decay conditions.

papers.title: Ridge Boosting is Both Robust and Efficient
papers.tldr: One ridge-regression boosting step achieves low bias and efficient variance across target shifts within an RKHS unit ball.

papers.title: Scalable and adaptive prediction bands with kernel sum-of-squares
papers.tldr: A kernel sum-of-squares approach makes prediction-band learning more scalable and introduces coverage-focused tuning for adaptivity.

papers.title: SD-KDE: Score-Debiased Kernel Density Estimation
papers.tldr: SD-KDE combines a single score-guided adjustment of each data point with a modified bandwidth to reduce density-estimation bias and error.

papers.title: Alignment-Sensitive Minimax Rates for Spectral Algorithms with Learned Kernels
papers.tldr: Effective span dimension connects learned spectral ordering to prediction risk and can decrease through feature learning under certain conditions.

papers.title: Conditional KRR: Injecting Unpenalized Features into Kernel Methods with Applications to Kernel Thresholding
papers.tldr: Conditional kernel ridge regression can improve prediction when selected unpenalized features capture a stronger target component than the remaining residual.

papers.title: Fast kernel methods: Sobolev, physics-informed, and additive models
papers.tldr: Fourier-based kernel regression achieves O(n log n) scaling and statistical guarantees, with current implementations constrained to low-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Kernel-based Maximum-of-difference Test for Two-sample Comparison
papers.tldr: The MOD test changes how kernel discrepancies are aggregated to improve sensitivity to distribution differences that can trouble MMD.

papers.title: On Uniform Error Bounds for Kernel Regression under Non-Gaussian Noise
papers.tldr: New finite-data kernel-regression error bounds accommodate broader noise distributions and correlations while providing tight uncertainty regions.
